nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of FeCoPd NPs
nodes.procedure: FeCl3·6H2O (0.5 mmol), PdCl2 (0.5 mmol) and CoCl2·6H2O (0.5 mmol) were dissolved in 7 mL deionized water in a beaker under constant magnetic stirring. After the dissolution of all the metal salts, 4.5 mL of hydrazine hydrate solution was added dropwise under constant vigorous stirring. Then previously prepared 1.0 M NaOH (20 mL) was added into the above resultant mixture under stirring to form a black coloured homogeneous mixture. The final reaction mixture was then transferred to a Teflon lined autoclave and kept at 200 °C for 6 hours. The as-prepared product was then naturally cooled to room temperature. The collected black coloured product was precipitated and washed with ethanol and dried at room temperature overnight for further studies.

nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of bimetallic NPs
nodes.procedure: Bimetallic FePd (FP), CoPd (CP) and FeCo (FC) NPs were synthesized using a similar synthetic technique as that utilized for FeCoPd NPs with equal amounts of metal salts (0.75 mmol each), but without the addition of the third metal salt. [Includes all details from FeCoPd synthesis with adjusted precursor amounts and compositions: for FP: FeCl3·6H2O (0.75 mmol) + PdCl2 (0.75 mmol); for CP: CoCl2·6H2O (0.75 mmol) + PdCl2 (0.75 mmol); for FC: FeCl3·6H2O (0.75 mmol) + CoCl2·6H2O (0.75 mmol); dissolved in 7 mL deionized water, 4.5 mL hydrazine hydrate added dropwise, 20 mL 1.0 M NaOH added, hydrothermal treatment at 200 °C for 6 h, washed with ethanol, dried at room temperature.]

FCP requires an η of 52, 146 and 190 mV... current density of 1000 mA cm⁻² at a 400 mV overpotential... Tafel slope value of 38 mV dec⁻¹... Rct is found to be lowest for FCP (0.97 Ω)... iex was found to be maximum... 147.07 mA cm⁻²... mass activity of FCP was found to be 4.67 A g⁻¹... TOF of 4.23 H₂ s⁻¹... durability up to a maximum of 66 h

The water oxidation reaction... was measured in a 1.0 M KOH aqueous electrolyte... FCP catalyst affords the lowest overpotential of 197 mV to acquire a current density of 10 mA cm⁻² and a maximum current density of 550 mA cm⁻² at a 540 mV overpotential... Tafel slope of FCP is found to be 47 mV dec⁻¹... Rct value of 1.55 Ω... Cdl value was found to be the maximum for FCP (1.954 mF)... ECSA value of 48.85 cm⁻²... durability for a minimum of 100 h
It also demonstrated OER stability in 30 wt% KOH with 180 mV overpotential at 10 mA cm⁻²

nodes.characterization_summary: FCP shows Pd fcc crystal structure with 2θ values at 40.18°, 46.65°, 68.30° and 82.20° corresponding to (111), (200), (220) and (311) planes, lattice parameter a = 3.89 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The 2θ value of FCP at 40.18, 46.65, 68.30 and 82.20° corresponds to the (111), (200), (220) and (311) planes which can be indexed to the Pd fcc structure having the space group Fm3m ... a = 3.89 Å.

nodes.characterization_summary: FCP shows polyhedral morphology with average particle size 20-40 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Polyhedral morphology of FCP is seen under low magnification transmission electron microscopy (TEM) imaging with an average particle size 20-40 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: FCP shows distinctive lattice fringes of (111) plane d = 0.22 nm and (200) plane d = 0.19 nm, single crystalline NPs grown in <111> and <100> directions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Distinctive lattice fringes of the (111) plane d = 0.22 nm are preponderantly observed under HRTEM ... lattice fringes of the (200) plane d = 0.19 nm are also observed.

nodes.characterization_summary: FCP shows octahedra and cuboctahedra morphology.
nodes.evidence_snippet: these polyhedral NPs are found to be octahedra and cuboctahedra under the field emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM) imaging.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern indexes lattice planes consistent with XRD results for Pd fcc structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Lattice planes similar to the XRD results were clearly indexed in the spotty selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern of the FCP sample.

nodes.characterization_summary: Homogeneous distribution of Fe, Co and Pd elements without phase segregation, atomic ratio nearly 1:1:1.
nodes.evidence_snippet: FESEM-EDS mapping had been carried out to analyse the distribution of Fe, Co and Pd in FCP ... All the elements were homogeneously distributed without any phase segregation.

nodes.characterization_summary: Type IV isotherm with surface area 16.03 m²/g, pore volume 0.112 cc/g, pore radius 1.1 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The detailed analysis of the surface properties investigated by using Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) N₂ adsorption–desorption at 77 K shows a type IV isotherm with a surface area of 16.03 m² g⁻¹ having a pore volume of 0.112 cc g⁻¹ and pore radius of 1.1 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows partial surface oxidation with oxidized Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺, Co²⁺/Co³⁺ peaks in fresh sample; after Ar⁺ sputtering metallic Fe⁰ (707.0 eV), Co⁰ (778.11, 792.96 eV), Pd⁰ peaks appear.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Oxidized metal ion peaks are seen in the initial assessment of the high-resolution XPS peaks of fresh FCP ... Metallic Fe, Co, and Pd signatures can be seen from the detailed XPS spectra in Fig. 2d–f besides their oxides due to the exposure to air.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS confirms integrity of Fe, Co, Pd metal concentrations in spent catalysts matching fresh FCP.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The elemental concentrations of Fe, Co and Pd in FCP were further analysed using inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) before and after HER and OER stability tests.
